name: Athens
operatingHours: Athens Metro runs ~5:30 AM–~12:30 AM Sun–Thu; Lines 1, 2 and 3 run until ~2:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays. Trains every 3–10 min by day, 10–15 min late at night.
fareInfo: Single ticket €1.20, valid 90 minutes across metro, tram, bus and trolleybus (excludes the airport). 24-hour pass €4.10, 5-day pass €8.20. The airport section of Line 3 beyond Koropi is a separate fare: €9 one way, €16 return (valid 30 days); the 3-day tourist pass with one airport round trip is €20. Visa/Mastercard contactless works on the whole network (€1.20 per ride, capped at €4.10 per day).

lines.name: Line 3 (M3)
lines.firstLast: Airport ↔ Syntagma: ~6:30 AM to ~11:30 PM, every ~36 min, ~40 min; airport ticket €9.

sights.name: Acropolis & Parthenon
sights.note: The 5th-century BC hilltop citadel crowned by the Parthenon, with the Erechtheion and the Temple of Athena Nike; the single most important sight in the city.
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–8:00 PM in summer, earlier close in winter (~5:00 PM); last entry 30 min before closing

sights.name: Acropolis Museum
sights.note: A glass-and-concrete museum at the foot of the hill holding the finds and sculptures from the Acropolis, with a glass floor over an excavated ancient neighbourhood.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; longer hours in summer and late opening on Fridays

sights.name: Plaka
sights.note: The oldest quarter of Athens, a maze of pedestrian lanes, neoclassical houses, tavernas and souvenir shops under the Acropolis.
sights.hours: Open streets; shops and tavernas ~10:00 AM–midnight

sights.name: Panathenaic Stadium
sights.note: The all-marble stadium that hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896; you can walk the track and visit the Olympic torch tunnel.

sights.name: Mount Lycabettus
sights.note: The pine-covered hill with a small chapel on top and a 360-degree view over the city to the sea; take the funicular or walk up from Kolonaki.

sights.name: National Archaeological Museum
sights.note: Greece's greatest antiquities collection, including the gold Mask of Agamemnon, the Antikythera mechanism and the bronze Poseidon.
sights.hours: ~8:30 AM–4:00 PM daily (reduced hours in winter); check site for Monday opening

sights.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
sights.note: The marketplace and civic heart of classical Athens, with the best-preserved Doric temple in Greece, the Temple of Hephaestus, and a reconstructed stoa museum.
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–8:00 PM in summer, earlier close in winter

sights.name: Anafiotika
sights.note: A tiny whitewashed corner of the Plaka built by island craftsmen, looking like a Cycladic village beneath the Acropolis cliff.

sights.name: Monastiraki Square & Flea Market
sights.note: The lively square beside the metro with a mosque, Hadrian's Library nearby and a flea market of antiques, leather and souvenirs along Ifestou street.
sights.hours: Square open always; flea market ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM, busiest on Sundays

sights.name: Benaki Museum
sights.note: A mansion museum tracing Greek art and culture from antiquity to the 20th century, with a rooftop café overlooking the National Garden.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM, closed Tue; to midnight Thu and Fri evenings

sights.name: National Garden
sights.note: A shady 19th-century park behind the Parliament, with palms, ponds and duck pools, handy for a break between museums.

sights.name: Philopappos Hill
sights.note: A free, wooded hill southwest of the Acropolis with a Roman-era monument and the best sunset view of the Parthenon.

sights.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
sights.note: The remaining Corinthian columns of what was once the largest temple in ancient Greece, next to Hadrian's Arch.
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–8:00 PM in summer, earlier close in winter

sights.name: Herod Atticus Odeon
sights.note: A 2nd-century Roman amphitheatre on the Acropolis slope, still used for concerts and the Athens Epidaurus Festival in summer; interior is open only with a performance ticket.
sights.hours: Visible from the Acropolis path; performances in summer evenings

sights.name: Athens Central Market (Varvakios)
sights.note: The noisy covered meat and fish market on Athinas street, with spice and cheese stalls and small ouzo bars around its edge.

sights.name: Changing of the Guard at Syntagma
sights.note: The ceremonial guard change by the Evzones in traditional dress in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier; a full ceremony runs Sundays at 11:00 AM.
sights.hours: Every hour on the hour daily; full ceremony Sun 11:00 AM

railStations.name: Larissa Station
railStations.note: Athens' main intercity station: Hellenic Train services north to Thessaloniki (~3.5 h) and beyond, plus suburban rail to the airport area and Corinth. Connects to Line 2 at Larissa Station metro stop.
railStations.hours: Intercity trains ~6:00 AM–~10:30 PM by timetable; Line 2 at the station ~5:30 AM–~12:30 AM.

airports.name: Athens International Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro Line 3 (blue) runs from the terminal to Syntagma in ~40 min, with onward service shown on this map; the airport section is a separate €9 fare. The X95 express bus to Syntagma (~€5.50, 60+ min) and taxis (flat ~€54 day / ~€70 night) are alternatives.
airports.hours: Line 3 airport service: first train ~5:30 AM, last ~11:30 PM (to ~12:30 AM Fri–Sat); express bus X95 runs 24 hours.
